williams-2026.title: 2025 Update to the Female Athlete Triad Coalition Consensus Statement Part 2: Clinical Guidelines for Screening, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Return to Play for Adolescents and Adults
williams-2026.support: Recent research supports the adoption of revised criteria for defining and treating energy deficiency, moving away from the concept of an energy-availability threshold. Energy deficiency-induced menstrual disturbances can be reversed with a moderate increase in food intake and modest weight gain, but restoration of menses alone is not associated with high rates of ovulation or increased ovarian steroid levels until multiple consecutive normal length menstrual cycles are achieved. Full text: an increase in energy intake between 300 and 600 kcal/day will likely initiate reproductive recovery; combined oral contraceptive pills may mask spontaneous menstrual resumption.

desouza-2026.title: 2025 Update to the Female Athlete Triad Coalition Consensus Statement Part 1: State of the Science and Introduction of a New Adolescent Model
desouza-2026.support: The Triad is defined as three inter-related components including energy status, reproductive function, and bone health. Full text: an EA of approximately 45 kcal/kg FFM/day has been associated with the healthy end of the Triad continuum; in this revised Consensus Statement, the utility of an EA threshold is less supported than in previous position stands; many women with ovulatory cycles had EA levels below 30 kcal/kg FFM/day, and women with menstrual disturbances had EA levels above 30.

mcdonald-deficit-size.title: Setting the Deficit - Small, Moderate or Large
mcdonald-deficit-size.support: Backs sizing the deficit as a percentage of maintenance, his small, moderate and large bands, and his view that small deficits need precise logging.

mcdonald-3500-rule.title: The 3500 Calorie Rule
mcdonald-3500-rule.support: Backs the points that early losses are mostly glycogen and water, and that a fixed cut stops working as expenditure adapts.

mcdonald-fat-loss-fundamentals.title: The Fundamentals of Fat Loss Diets Part 1
mcdonald-fat-loss-fundamentals.support: Backs the set-up order of calories, protein, fat and then carbohydrate, with fat kept moderate for adherence.

mcdonald-athletes-fat-loss.title: Fat Loss for Athletes: Part 1
mcdonald-athletes-fat-loss.support: Backs keeping food around hard sessions while dieting, taking carbohydrate cuts from other meals, and dieting in a general preparation block.

purcell-2014.title: The effect of rate of weight loss on long-term weight management: a randomised controlled trial
purcell-2014.support: Both gradual weight loss and rapid weight loss participants who completed the study had regained most of their lost weight (gradual weight loss 71.2% regain vs rapid weight loss 70.5%). The rate of weight loss does not affect the proportion of weight regained within 144 weeks.

nackers-2010.title: The Association Between Rate of Initial Weight Loss and Long-Term Success in Obesity Treatment: Does Slow and Steady Win the Race?
nackers-2010.support: The FAST and SLOW groups differed significantly at 18 months (-10.9, -7.1, and -3.7 kg). Fast weight losers obtained greater weight reduction and long-term maintenance, and were not more susceptible to weight regain than gradual weight losers.

hall-2016.title: Energy expenditure and body composition changes after an isocaloric ketogenic diet in overweight and obese men
hall-2016.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
hall-2016.support: Compared with BD, the KD coincided with increased EEchamber (57 +/- 13 kcal/d). Body fat loss slowed during the KD and coincided with increased protein utilization and loss of fat-free mass.

thomas-2013.title: Can a weight loss of one pound a week be achieved with a 3500-kcal deficit? Commentary on a commonly accepted rule
thomas-2013.support: Abstract: the 3500-kcal rule grossly overestimates actual weight loss in seven experiments with supervised or objectively measured intake. Full text: 103 adults lost 20.1 lb against 27.6 lb predicted by the rule, over about 65 days.

manore-2015.title: Weight Management for Athletes and Active Individuals: A Brief Review
manore-2015.support: Key points: avoiding severe energy restriction; timing of food intake around exercise and spreading meals/snacks throughout the day. Full text: identify a healthy body weight the athlete can maintain for most of the year.

cfr-101-9.title: 21 CFR 101.9 Nutrition labeling of food, paragraph (g)(5)
cfr-101-9.support: A food with a label declaration of calories ... shall be deemed misbranded if the nutrient content of the composite is greater than 20 percent in excess of the value declared on the label.

urban-2011.title: Accuracy of Stated Energy Contents of Restaurant Foods
urban-2011.support: 269 items from 42 restaurants; 50 (19%) contained at least 100 kcal/portion more than stated.

burrows-2019.title: Validity of Dietary Assessment Methods When Compared to the Method of Doubly Labeled Water: A Systematic Review in Adults
burrows-2019.support: 59 studies with 6,298 free living adults; the majority reported significant under-reporting of energy intake compared with doubly labeled water.

heymsfield-2012.title: Energy content of weight loss: kinetic features during voluntary caloric restriction
heymsfield-2012.support: Delta EC/Delta W (kilocalories per kilogram) increased significantly from week 4 (4,858 +/- 388) to 6 (6,041 +/- 376) and changed insignificantly thereafter, in 23 overweight men and women evaluated by DXA.

madero-2011.title: The effect of two energy-restricted diets, a low-fructose diet versus a moderate natural fructose diet, on weight loss and metabolic syndrome parameters: a randomized controlled trial
madero-2011.support: Weight loss was higher in the moderate natural fructose group (4.19 +/- 0.30 kg) than the low-fructose group (2.83 +/- 0.29 kg) over 6 weeks; low-fructose diet under 20 g/d vs moderate-fructose diet with natural fruit supplements 50-70 g/d.

westenhoefer-1999.title: Validation of the flexible and rigid control dimensions of dietary restraint
westenhoefer-1999.support: Rigid control is associated with higher BMI and more frequent and more severe binge eating episodes. Flexible control is associated with lower BMI, less binge eating and a higher probability of successful weight reduction during the 1-year program.

stewart-2002.title: Rigid vs. flexible dieting: association with eating disorder symptoms in nonobese women
stewart-2002.support: Individuals who engage in rigid dieting strategies reported symptoms of an eating disorder, mood disturbances, and excessive concern with body size/shape; flexible dieting strategies were not highly associated with these.

mcdonald-hunger.title: 9 Ways to Deal with Hunger on a Diet
mcdonald-hunger.support: Backs keeping whole fruit and moderate fat in a fat-loss diet for fullness, and treating small lapses as minor.

mcdonald-rigid-flexible.title: Rigid vs. Flexible Dieting
mcdonald-rigid-flexible.support: Backs his view that all-or-nothing food rules turn small lapses into large ones, and his preference for planned free meals over the label cheat.

mcdonald-rapid-fat-loss.title: Is Rapid Fat Loss Right For You?
mcdonald-rapid-fat-loss.support: Backs his 2009 argument that fast initial loss need not mean worse long-term results if the diet uses whole food, exercise and a plan for maintenance.

mcdonald-calorie-a-calorie.title: Is a Calorie a Calorie?
mcdonald-calorie-a-calorie.support: Backs the point that fast early losses on low-carbohydrate diets are water, and that matched-calorie diets differ little once protein is adequate.

mcdonald-principles-details.title: Fundamental Principles vs. Minor Details
mcdonald-principles-details.support: Backs settling calories and protein before any finer detail of diet set-up.

mcdonald-detail-oriented.title: How Detail Oriented Do You Need to Be
mcdonald-detail-oriented.support: Backs his rule of replacing a change that shows nothing after about four weeks and leaving a working plan alone.

mcdonald-maintenance.title: How to Estimate Maintenance Caloric Intake
mcdonald-maintenance.support: Backs treating any maintenance estimate as a starting point that must be corrected against real change.

mcdonald-holiday.title: 10 Ways to Deal with Holiday Weight Gain
mcdonald-holiday.support: Backs planning treats, filling up on protein and vegetables first, and ignoring the scale spike after a large meal.

mcdonald-contest-dieting.title: Contest Dieting Part 1
mcdonald-contest-dieting.support: Backs his view that dropping dairy in contest prep is a habit without a basis, and that dairy supplies calcium.

mcdonald-insulin-levels.title: Insulin Levels and Fat Loss
mcdonald-insulin-levels.support: Backs the definition of the glycaemic index and the point that GI-driven insulin differences matter little for fat burning.

mcdonald-comparing-diets-1.title: Comparing the Diets: Part 1
mcdonald-comparing-diets-1.support: Backs the point that diet percentages mislead because requirements follow body size.

mcdonald-comparing-diets-2.title: Comparing the Diets: Part 2
mcdonald-comparing-diets-2.support: Backs the definitions of the targeted and cyclical ketogenic diets.

mcdonald-percentages.title: Diet Percentages: Part 1
mcdonald-percentages.support: Backs setting protein in grams per unit of body weight rather than as a share of calories.

mcdonald-meal-patterning.title: Meal Frequency and Meal Patterning Part 1 - Book Excerpt
mcdonald-meal-patterning.support: Backs his view that smaller dieters often do better with fewer, larger meals or with calories moved to the evening.

mcdonald-meal-frequency.title: Meal Frequency and Energy Balance
mcdonald-meal-frequency.support: Backs the point that the thermic effect of food depends on total intake, not on how often you eat.

yanovski-2000.title: A Prospective Study of Holiday Weight Gain
yanovski-2000.support: The mean weight increased significantly during the holiday period (gain, 0.37+/-1.52 kg). Since this gain is not reversed during the spring or summer months, the net 0.48-kg weight gain in the fall and winter probably contributes to the increase in body weight that frequently occurs during adulthood.

chen-2012.title: Effects of dairy intake on body weight and fat: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
chen-2012.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
chen-2012.support: Overall, consumption of dairy products did not result in a significant reduction in weight (-0.14 kg). Consumption of dairy products reduced body weight in the context of energy restriction or short-term intervention; 22 RCTs on body fat showed a modest reduction (-0.45 kg).

diaz-2006.title: Glycaemic index effects on fuel partitioning in humans
diaz-2006.support: Several studies comparing meals with contrasting glycaemic carbohydrates for hours, days or weeks have failed to demonstrate any differential effect on fuel partitioning. Apparently, the glycaemic index-induced serum insulin differences are not sufficient in magnitude and/or duration to modify fuel oxidation.

sievert-2019.title: Effect of breakfast on weight and energy intake: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
sievert-2019.support: A small difference in weight favouring participants who skipped breakfast (mean difference 0.44 kg). Participants assigned to breakfast had a higher total daily energy intake than those assigned to skip breakfast (mean difference 259.79 kcal/day).

mcdonald-full-diet-break.title: The Full Diet Break
mcdonald-full-diet-break.support: Backs his diet-break practice: 10 to 14 days near maintenance, a carbohydrate floor, closer spacing for leaner dieters, and planning breaks around holidays to keep control.

mcdonald-training-vs-diet.title: Does the Diet Determine the Training or Vice Versa
mcdonald-training-vs-diet.support: Backs his view that low days of alternate-day or intermittent restriction plans belong on rest days, and that fixed training days rule some patterns out.

mcdonald-energy-balance.title: The Energy Balance Equation
mcdonald-energy-balance.support: Backs his view that differences in digestion and gut bacteria alter the energy-in term without breaking energy balance.

wing-2003.title: Prescribed “Breaks” as a Means to Disrupt Weight Control Efforts
wing-2003.support: Breaks produced a slowing of weight loss or slight regain, but weight losses during the breaks were not significantly different from the control group. Importantly, overall weight losses (0 to 5 months or 0 to 11 months) did not differ between conditions.

pasquali-1982.title: Effect of dietary carbohydrates during hypocaloric treatment of obesity on peripheral thyroid hormone metabolism
pasquali-1982.support: A fall in T3 levels during the entire period of study with respect to the basal levels occurred only when the CHO of the diet was 120 g/day or less, independent of caloric intake (360, 645 or 1200 calories).

westerterp-plantenga-2004.title: High protein intake sustains weight maintenance after body weight loss in humans
westerterp-plantenga-2004.support: A 20% higher protein intake, that is, 18% of energy vs 15% of energy during weight maintenance after weight loss, resulted in a 50% lower body weight regain, only consisting of fat-free mass, and related to increased satiety and decreased energy efficiency.

trexler-2017.title: Physiological Changes Following Competition in Male and Female Physique Athletes: A Pilot Study
trexler-2017.journal: International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism
trexler-2017.support: FM (T1 = 7.7 ± 4.4 kg, T2 = 8.0 ± 4.4, T3 = 10.0 ± 6.2; T3 > T1 and T2). TBW increased from T1 to T2. RMR and male testosterone increased while FM was preferentially gained 4-6 weeks postcompetition.

jumpertz-2011.title: Energy-balance studies reveal associations between gut microbes, caloric load, and nutrient absorption in humans
jumpertz-2011.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
jumpertz-2011.support: These changes were directly correlated with stool energy loss in lean individuals such that a 20% increase in Firmicutes and a corresponding decrease in Bacteroidetes were associated with an increased energy harvest of ≈150 kcal.

harvie-2011.title: The effects of intermittent or continuous energy restriction on weight loss and metabolic disease risk markers: a randomized trial in young overweight women
harvie-2011.support: 107 overweight or obese premenopausal women over 6 months: about 2,710 kJ a day on 2 days a week lost as much weight as a daily 25% restriction.

mcdonald-what-are-calories.title: What are Calories?
mcdonald-what-are-calories.support: Backs the idea of balance for each nutrient (intake minus oxidation), and his view that alcohol has no store in the body and is burned off first.

mcdonald-best-diet.title: What's the Best Diet - Book Teaser
mcdonald-best-diet.support: Backs his short list of what any fat-loss diet must provide and what makes it workable, and his view that low-carb diets may succeed mainly through higher protein.

mcdonald-not-different.title: You Are Not Different
mcdonald-not-different.support: Backs the point that people differ in how hard the body resists a surplus or deficit, while no one escapes energy balance.

mcdonald-intro-dieting.title: An Introduction to Dieting
mcdonald-intro-dieting.support: Backs his view that diet-approved processed foods carry plenty of calories and invite people to eat more of them, which helps bring on a plateau.

mcdonald-causes-diet-failure.title: What Are the Causes of Diet Failure?
mcdonald-causes-diet-failure.support: Backs his view that unrealistic goals and false expectations of quick, easy loss drive people to quit, and that higher protein is the most useful single diet change.

abbott-1988.title: Short-term energy balance: relationship with protein, carbohydrate, and fat balances
abbott-1988.journal: American Journal of Physiology-Endocrinology and Metabolism
abbott-1988.support: There were no correlations between energy balance and either carbohydrate or protein balances. Thus fat, rather than carbohydrate or protein, is almost exclusively used or stored in response to day-to-day fluctuations in energy balance.

suter-1992.title: The Effect of Ethanol on Fat Storage in Healthy Subjects
suter-1992.support: Both the addition of ethanol and the isocaloric substitution of ethanol for other foods reduced 24-hour lipid oxidation (reductions of 36 +/- 3 percent and 31 +/- 7 percent). Neither significantly altered the oxidation of carbohydrate or protein.

soenen-2012.title: Relatively high-protein or ‘low-carb’ energy-restricted diets for body weight loss and body weight maintenance?
soenen-2012.support: Body-weight loss and weight-maintenance depends on the high-protein, but not on the 'low-carb' component of the diet, while it is unrelated to the concomitant fat-content of the diet.

shide-1995.title: Information About the Fat Content of Preloads Influences Energy Intake in Healthy Women
shide-1995.journal: Journal of the American Dietetic Association
shide-1995.support: Subjects who had information consumed more energy at lunch after eating a preload labeled low fat than after eating a preload with similar energy content but labeled high fat. When energy consumed at dinner was included, overall intake was still significantly greater.

bouchard-1990.title: The Response to Long-Term Overfeeding in Identical Twins
bouchard-1990.support: 12 pairs of young adult male monozygotic twins were overfed by 4.2 MJ (1000 kcal) per day, 6 days a week, for a total of 84 days. The mean weight gain was 8.1 kg, but the range was 4.3 to 13.3 kg, with about three times more variance among pairs than within pairs.

foster-1997.title: What is a reasonable weight loss? Patients' expectations and evaluations of obesity treatment outcomes.
foster-1997.journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
foster-1997.support: Goal weight averaged a 32% reduction in body weight. A 17-kg weight loss was defined as disappointed. After 48 weeks of treatment and a 16-kg weight loss, 47% of patients did not achieve even a disappointed weight.

polivy-2002.title: If at first you don't succeed: False hopes of self-change.
polivy-2002.support: The authors have described this cycle of failure and renewed effort as a 'false hope syndrome' characterized by unrealistic expectations about the likely speed, amount, ease, and consequences of self-change attempts.

mcdonald-metabolic-damage.title: Permanent Metabolic Damage - Q&A
mcdonald-metabolic-damage.support: Backs his view that formerly obese people keep a small but lasting drop in resting metabolic rate, and that claims of gaining fat on very low intakes are implausible.

mcdonald-keto-advantage.title: Ketogenic Low-Carbohydrate Diets and Metabolic Advantage
mcdonald-keto-advantage.support: Backs his reading of a controlled 6-week trial with protein held near equal, and his view that low carb's real edge for some people is control of appetite and food choice.

mcdonald-dieters-paradox.title: The Dieters Paradox - Research Review
mcdonald-dieters-paradox.support: Backs the term for believing a healthy side dish lowers a meal's calories, and his view that sorting foods into good and bad distracts from portions.

mcdonald-training-dieting.title: Weight Training for Fat Loss Part 1
mcdonald-training-dieting.support: Backs his practice of cutting heavy volume by up to two thirds while keeping the load during a diet, and adding light high-rep work only in the time saved.

mcdonald-antidepressants.title: Antidepressants and Weight Gain
mcdonald-antidepressants.support: Backs his view that antidepressant classes differ in their effect on weight, mainly through appetite and sometimes activity.

mcdonald-dieting-surgery.title: Dieting and Surgery - Q&A
mcdonald-dieting-surgery.support: Backs his advice to heal before dieting after surgery or injury, eating at maintenance or slightly above while recovering.

astrup-1999.title: Meta-analysis of resting metabolic rate in formerly obese subjects
astrup-1999.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
astrup-1999.support: RMR adjusted for differences in fat-free mass and fat mass was 2.9% lower in formerly obese subjects than in control subjects (P = 0.09). In the traditional meta-analysis relative RMR was lower by 5.1%. Formerly obese subjects had a 3-5% lower mean relative RMR than control subjects.

johnston-2006.title: Ketogenic low-carbohydrate diets have no metabolic advantage over nonketogenic low-carbohydrate diets
johnston-2006.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
johnston-2006.support: Mean weight losses (6.3 and 7.2 kg in KLC and NLC dieters; P = 0.324) and fat losses (3.4 and 5.5 kg; P = 0.111) did not differ significantly by group after 6 wk. Inflammatory risk and perceptions of vigor were more adversely affected by the KLC than by the NLC diet.

chernev-2011.title: The Dieter's Paradox
chernev-2011.support: People erroneously believe that eating healthy foods in addition to unhealthy ones can decrease a meal's calorie count. This misperception is stronger among individuals most concerned with managing their weight.

bickel-2011.title: Exercise Dosing to Retain Resistance Training Adaptations in Young and Older Adults
bickel-2011.support: RT 3 d/wk for 16 wk followed by 32 wk of detraining or a maintenance dose of one-third or one-ninth. Both maintenance prescriptions preserved phase 1 muscle hypertrophy in the young but not the old.

serretti-2010.title: Antidepressants and Body Weight
serretti-2010.support: Amitriptyline, mirtazapine, and paroxetine were associated with a greater risk of weight gain. Some weight loss occurs with fluoxetine and bupropion, although the effect of fluoxetine appears limited to the acute phase. The effect of each antidepressant may vary greatly depending on an individual's characteristics.
